hero.title: Found pattern
hero.description: Use this module to list found dogs: a card grid of notices with status filtering. It lists notices only; any guidance a rescue offers the public is its own page content.

example.title: Example

source.title: Snippet
source.description: Where a notice came from, such as a Facebook post, is recorded as an inline comment on the entry in the site's data file. When the original post or another source exists, set `source.url` (and optionally `source.name`) and the card links to it in a new tab; leave it unset to link nowhere.

standard.title: Standard
items: Use `FoundListingsSection` for all found-notice pages; it only lists found dogs.
Keep listing data normalized in `FoundListing` objects (`pet`, `location`, `source`, `status`).
Use mode controls (`local`, `external`, `hybrid`) instead of page-local filtering logic.

Do not add public-guidance content to the module (hold-the-dog warnings, notice checklists, reunification steps, submit-a-notice buttons, trapping advice). A site that offers those services writes them as page-local content around the list (Rovers Return Dog Rescue is the reference).
Source/media links should open in a new tab with safe rel attributes.
Use neutral styling defaults (no site-specific color branding in shared standards).
Use `statusFilter` plus `showReunited`/`showArchived` (both default `false`) to control found-notice lifecycle visibility: active notices show by default; reunited/archived are opt-in.
Cards render from normalized `FoundListing` metadata with a generic heading (`labels.noticeTitle`, no notice number); image and source links open safely in a new tab.

Expiry is mandatory: every notice carries a required ISO `foundAtISO` (the Facebook post date, printed on the card as "Posted:" and the date the expiry counts from), and an `open`/`hold` notice stops rendering 30 days after it (hidden, never deleted; the entry stays in the data file). A site changes the window for its whole list with `expireAfterDays` (a positive whole number; it cannot be turned off), and a single notice can override it with `expiresAt` (ISO date, hidden after that day). `reunited`/`archived` notices shown through `showReunited`/`showArchived` are not expired.
Use `gender` on the pet profile: it matches the field name used across every other pattern (`AdoptablePetsSection`, kennel-display tools).
Source: set `source.url` (and `source.name`, for example "Facebook") to the original post when it exists so the card links to it in a new tab; leave it unset to link nowhere.

Each notice can carry any number of images in `media`: one shows as a plain image, two or more become a carousel with arrows and a count (`MediaCarouselTile`). Clicking an image opens it full-size in a new tab, and images are never cropped.
